extracted.intended_audience: astronomers / observatory staff / readers of an observatory report
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting and reducing positional observations of stars in an observatory report—what to state, how to reduce microscope means, and which instrumental matters to record. Applies to preparing tables and summaries of culminations, microscope means, and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: State number and quality of observations
rubrics_metrics.description: the number and quality of observations upon which they are founded should always be stated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted guidance: "in order that their due weight may be attached to them in comparisons with succeeding observations." In other words, when giving determinations of positions of stars or geographical places, report how many observations were used and their quality so readers can assess the weight of the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply refraction and reduction corrections to microscope means
rubrics_metrics.description: the sums or differences of [the refraction and reduction] means have been applied to the means of the microscopes, so that the latter corrected means are the divisions of the mural circle corresponding to the superior and inferior culminations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note from the report: columns of Refraction and Reduction were omitted for want of room, but their means were still applied to microscope means. When publishing, either show the correction columns or state explicitly that the refraction/reduction means have been applied to the microscope means and how.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report mean values and number of observations for microscope results
rubrics_metrics.description: Mean of 4 Microscopes .. .  by  N Observ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report consistently gives a 'Mean of 4 Microscopes' (or other group) followed by the number of observations. When combining multiple microscopes, present the group mean and the count of observations used (e.g. "Mean of 4 Microscopes . 1° 34' 41" . 82 by 31 Observ.").

rubrics_metrics.name: Report measurement dispersion (half differences / S. P. D.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Half Diff. S. P. D.  (and Mean S. P. D.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tables present 'Half Diff. S. P. D.' and 'Mean S. P. D.' values alongside means; include measures of dispersion or half-differences so readers can judge internal consistency of microscope observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note instrumental anomalies and periods of derangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The second microscope during the years of 1822 and 1823 was subject to frequent derangements, from causes over which I had no control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document any known instrument problems, with dates and affected instruments, because they affect data quality and interpretation. If an instrument was unreliable during particular years, state that explicitly in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: State that mural-circle divisions vary but differences are constant
rubrics_metrics.description: These divisions are variable, because the position of the tube is altered and the pillar settles; but their differences are constant quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain which quantities are expected to vary (e.g. absolute divisions of the mural circle due to mechanical changes) and which are stable (e.g. differences between divisions). Make clear which values are used for reduction and which for comparative purposes.
